answer: Every epoch, at a random minute past dawn, the network drops puzzles into the river of pending work, each seeded uniquely so no two identities ever see the same one. An identity keeps its earnings only if it solves its own puzzle before the 90-minute horizon closes, checked automatically against the seed. Each puzzle takes a human eight minutes, so one operator can cover at most eleven identities per window, and hired solvers cost $2 each. A hundred fakes costs $200 an epoch, and a missed window freezes that identity's rewards for three epochs.
